The following two claims conclude the proof of Lemma 4. A. Entropy The usual Shannon entropyof a random variable X is defined by H(X) := x∈supp(X) p(x) log(1/p(x)) where p(x) := Pr[x = x]. Given two random variables X and Y , we define the conditional entropy of X given Y by H(X | Y ) := Ey∼Y [H(X | Y = y)]. A simple form of the chain rule for entropy states that H(XY ) = H(X) + H(Y | X). For convenience, if X ⊆ {0, 1}n is a set, we write X ∼ X for the random variable that is uniformly distributed over X. In particular, XT denotes the random variable X marginalised onto coordinates T ⊆ [n]. For more background on entropy, we refer to [CT05].
